types.name: Best diagram for three classes
types.description: Three or four class names are given (for example "Mothers, Women, Doctors") and you choose the Venn diagram that best shows how they are related.

types.name: Numbers in a circle diagram
types.description: A diagram of labelled circles has numbers in its parts, and you add or compare numbers for a description such as "singers and dancers but not actors".

types.name: Shapes standing for groups
types.description: Shapes such as a triangle, square, circle or pentagon each "represent" or "stand for" a group, and you find the number or letter in the region that fits a description.

types.name: Diagram for given statements
types.description: Statements such as "All A are B, some B are C" are given and you pick the Venn diagram that represents them.

types.name: Counting with two or three sets
types.description: A word problem gives how many people like or do each thing and how many do both, and asks for "neither", "only one" or the total, with no figure needed.
